cues.en: Keeping with the theme of exploring real-world lessons in recommender systems, let's do a deeper dive into a couple of case studies from two of the best known recommender systems out there, YouTube and Netflix.
cues.zh: 延續探討推薦系統實務經驗的主題，來深入研究兩個最知名推薦系統的案例：YouTube 與 Netflix。

cues.en: Let's start with diving into how recommendations work with YouTube.
cues.zh: 先深入了解 YouTube 推薦如何運作。

cues.en: YouTube is now owned by Google, and given Google's obsession with deep learning, it shouldn't surprise you that YouTube has gone all in with deep learning to power its recommendations.
cues.zh: YouTube 現在屬於 Google，而考量 Google 對深度學習的熱衷，YouTube 全面採用深度學習驅動推薦，應該不令人意外。

cues.en: A nice thing about Google is that they publish a lot of their research, and open-source a lot of their internal tools.
cues.zh: Google 有個好處，就是會發表許多研究，也將很多內部工具開放原始碼。

cues.en: As a business person I'd criticize them for enabling their competitors, but as an educator I think this is a wonderful thing.
cues.zh: 以商人的角度，我會批評這是在幫助競爭對手，但以教育者的角度，我認為這很棒。

cues.en: They've made the paper Deep Neural Networks for YouTube Recommendations freely available, and it goes into quite a bit of detail on how YouTube recommendations work.
cues.zh: 他們免費公開了 Deep Neural Networks for YouTube Recommendations 這篇論文，詳細介紹 YouTube 推薦的運作方式。

cues.en: Not only is this a treasure trove of insight for researchers in recommender systems, but it also contains valuable information for people trying to optimize their own YouTube channels.
cues.zh: 這不只是推薦系統研究人員的知識寶庫，也為想最佳化自己 YouTube 頻道的人，提供寶貴資訊。

cues.en: Let's go over some of the more interesting points in the paper.
cues.zh: 來看論文中一些較有趣的重點。

cues.en: YouTube has some specific challenges, so keep these in mind before you decide to apply what they did to your own problems.
cues.zh: YouTube 有一些特定挑戰，所以在決定把他們的做法用於自己的問題前，要先記住這些挑戰。

cues.en: If you don't have the same problems, the same solution may not be the appropriate one for you.
cues.zh: 如果面對的問題不同，相同解法可能不適合你。

cues.en: The first issue is scale, YouTube has well over one billion users, who watch five billion videos every day.
cues.zh: 第一個問題是規模。YouTube 有遠超過十億位使用者，每天觀看五十億部影片。

cues.en: That's just mind boggling when you think about how many users and items they have to compute recommendations for.
cues.zh: 想到必須為多少使用者與項目計算推薦，真的令人難以想像。

cues.en: Anything they do must be horizontally scaled and distributed on a massive cluster, and must be vended to the users extremely efficiently.
cues.zh: 所有工作都必須在龐大叢集上水平擴展、分散執行，並以極高效率提供給使用者。

cues.en: The next is freshness, over 300 hours of video are uploaded to YouTube every minute, and their recommendations must take into account both newly uploaded content,
cues.zh: 接著是新鮮度。每分鐘有超過 300 小時的影片上傳到 YouTube，推薦必須同時考慮新上傳的內容，

cues.en: and up-to-the-second data on each users' individual actions that might indicate their interests right now.
cues.zh: 以及精確到秒的個別使用者行為資料，判斷他們此刻的興趣。

cues.en: They must strike a deliberate balance between recommending well-established videos, and new content but they clearly favor new content.
cues.zh: 他們必須刻意平衡成熟影片與新內容的推薦，但明顯偏重新內容。

cues.en: The last big issue is noise, most of their interest data consists of implicit ratings, not explicit ratings.
cues.zh: 最後一個大問題是雜訊。大部分興趣資料都是隱含評分，而非明確評分。

cues.en: As we talked about in the previous section, implicit ratings data is fraught with peril, just basing recommendations on which videos people click on creates a system that's subject to gaming
cues.zh: 就像上一節談過的，隱含評分資料充滿風險。只根據人們點擊哪些影片推薦，會讓系統容易被操弄，

cues.en: and, in the words of the paper, unobservable external factors.
cues.zh: 以及受到論文所說的「無法觀測的外部因素」影響。

cues.en: Someone clicking on a viral video isn't necessarily an indication of the ground truth of that user's interests.
cues.zh: 某人點擊一部爆紅影片，不一定能反映他的真實興趣。

cues.en: Their data is also extremely sparse, and the content attributes associated with their videos is quote poorly structured without a well-defined ontology unquote.
cues.zh: 資料也非常稀疏，影片的內容屬性則是，引用原文，「結構不佳，而且沒有明確定義的本體」。

cues.en: That's YouTube's polite way of saying that the data they're working with is a real mess.
cues.zh: 這是 YouTube 委婉地說，他們處理的資料非常混亂。

cues.en: Based on their results, it seems they've done a good job of overcoming these challenges.
cues.zh: 從結果來看，他們似乎成功克服了這些挑戰。

cues.en: When I visit the YouTube homepage, it comes up instantly and includes recommendations that do an excellent job of capturing my current interests.
cues.zh: 我造訪 YouTube 首頁時，頁面會立即出現，而且推薦非常準確地掌握我目前的興趣。

cues.en: Google has gone all-in with deep learning, with a mandate to use it for nearly every machine learning problem they encounter.
cues.zh: Google 全面投入深度學習，要求遇到的幾乎所有機器學習問題，都使用深度學習。

cues.en: I can understand why they did this, it allows them to focus all of their engineering effort on deep learning frameworks, and use that as a general purpose tool for use by the rest of Google and its child companies,
cues.zh: 我能理解原因。這讓他們能將所有工程心力集中於深度學習框架，作為通用工具，供 Google 其他部門與旗下公司使用，

cues.en: such as YouTube.
cues.zh: 例如 YouTube。

cues.en: So, in 2016 YouTube moved its recommendations to a deep learning framework, powered by Google Brain, which today is called TensorFlow!
cues.zh: 因此在 2016 年，YouTube 將推薦移到由 Google Brain 驅動的深度學習框架，也就是今天所稱的 TensorFlow！

cues.en: Previously, their approach was based on matrix factorization, which we've also covered.
cues.zh: 以前的方法以矩陣分解為基礎，這也是我們介紹過的。

cues.en: As we've mentioned in the course, you can implement matrix factorization with a neural network, and at first that's exactly what they did.
cues.zh: 課程提過，可以用神經網路實作矩陣分解，而他們一開始正是這麼做。

cues.en: But over time, their approach evolved beyond matrix factorization.
cues.zh: 但隨著時間，方法演進，超越了矩陣分解。
